findings: The original ZIP lacked predictive maintenance, fraud, and healthcare readmission scenarios.
The blueprint now includes five stakeholder-led synthetic scenarios and multi-turn conversations.
Tool identifiers are included in preceding context and arguments are validated against the registered tool schemas.
Serialized tool results include the complete ToolResult shape; handoff and engine-inspection payloads are schema-validated.
SQL and Python KPI examples execute against synthetic fixtures; DAX examples are checked for required measures and fields.
Zero-spend marketing and fully-refunded e-commerce groups exercise undefined-denominator behavior.
Maintenance outcome labels are prediction-observation grain and must not be interpreted as unique failure-event counts.
decisions.name: training_examples

findings: The suite contains scenario-specific profiles, mandatory facts, incorrect behaviors, acceptance/rejection criteria, and case-specific 100-point rubrics.
Five required stakeholder prompts are included.
Individual evaluation records remain draft, and tool execution requires a workflow-aware runner.
The text suite remains a smoke-test scaffold, not an approved final model-comparison benchmark.
decisions.name: human_evaluation_suite

conditions: All figures are synthetic descriptive calculations and must not be presented as production evidence.

Marketing ROAS is attribution-based, not causal; last-click and a 30-day window are declared assumptions that cannot be independently audited from aggregate rows. Impressions are absent, so CTR is unavailable.
E-commerce net line sales use line grain and explicit discounts, refunds, cancellations, and COGS; tax and shipping are absent, and a fully-refunded group exercises undefined margin.
Maintenance risk is not a confirmed failure; rolling features must end at prediction time, and repeated positive observation rows are not unique failure-event counts.
Fraud labels require completed review; flagged transactions remain suspicious, not confirmed fraud.
Healthcare rates use eligible discharges with complete follow-up; predictions require discharge-time features and human clinical review.
